subject: Subprocessor change notice & request for onward-transfer consent
messages:
From: FinCo Legal <legal@finco.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: current subprocessor roster + onward-transfer permissions

Hi Lauren,

As part of our annual vendor review and GDPR DPA obligations, can you send us the current list of subprocessors (names, locations, processing purpose) that Redwood uses to support FinCo Payments? Specifically: whether any subprocessors will process EU personal data outside the EEA, and whether Redwood requires our explicit consent for any onward transfers.

We also need copies of any recent notices of subprocessor changes and a copy of the DPA addendum referenced during procurement (we have a pending renewal).

Can you confirm by EOD next Friday (2026-02-16)? If any new subprocessors have been added in the last 90 days, we may require prior notice or explicit consent per section 4.3 of our DPA.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Legal – FinCo Payments
legal@finco.com

[Attachment: vendor_subpo_request_guidance.pdf (PDF)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: FinCo Legal <legal@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + onward-transfer permissions

Marta —

Thanks for the note. Attached is our latest subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_2026-02-15.csv) and the DPA addendum we use as a starting point (DPA addendum stub attached). Quick summary:

- No changes in the roster since our last update except one planned addition (DataStream Inc.) that we intend to onboard for telemetry aggregation.
- DataStream Inc. is a Singapore-based analytics provider. They will only process aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry (no cleartext PII).
- We anticipate the onboarding to be completed in late Feb; we planned to provide notice, but are raising this explicitly because of your DPA clause.
- Regarding onward transfers: our standard approach is to provide notification for new subprocessors; we request explicit consent only for subprocessors that will process personal data outside jurisdictions covered by SCCs and where the processing is high-risk. For DataStream, we propose to proceed under SCCs + the DPA addendum; if FinCo requires explicit prior consent instead of tacit approval, we understand and will pause onboarding until a signed addendum is completed.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2026-02-15.csv (CSV), DPA_addendum_stub.pdf (PDF)

Let us know if you want a one-pager mapping each subprocessor to the DPA clauses. If you'd like, we can also schedule a quick call with Marissa (security) and Karthik (procurement) this week.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: subprocessor_roster_2026-02-15.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: DPA_addendum_stub.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, FinCo Legal <legal@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 13:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + onward-transfer permissions

Marta / Lauren —

Following up with a little more color from the security & procurement side on DataStream Inc.:

- Reason for selection: real-time telemetry consolidation for autoscaling metrics; reduces tokenization overhead and is expected to lower per-token cost by ~8%.
- Data types: aggregated usage counters, anonymized request latencies, and service health signals. No message content or identifiable user IDs will be shared.
- Controls in place: contractual encryption-at-rest, RBAC limited to analytics team, and a 12-month data retention policy followed by automated purging.
- Location: Singapore (multi-tenant cloud). We will require DataStream to accept SCCs and sign Redwood's DPA addendum.

If FinCo prefers not to allow any subprocessor outside the EEA that processes telemetry even in pseudonymized form, we can offer a configuration to route FinCo traffic through EU-only telemetry pipelines for an additional monthly fee — let me know and we can share updated pricing.

Procurement note (cc Karthik): if FinCo requires explicit prior consent and a signed addendum before the vendor is onboarded, procurement will expedite DocuSign and we can block onboarding until sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[Attachment: subprocessor_onboarding_summary_DataStream_2026-02-16.pdf (PDF)]

From: FinCo Legal <legal@finco.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Alan Smith <alan.smith@vendorx.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + onward-transfer permissions

Lauren / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the roster. We've reviewed the materials and, given DataStream's Singapore location, FinCo requires explicit prior consent for any subprocessor that will process EU personal data outside the EEA, even if pseudonymized.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
1) Provide a signed DPA addendum that includes the SCCs mapping (we will countersign).
2) Start a DocuSign envelope for the addendum and the standard subprocessor clause acknowledgement.
3) Confirm that DataStream will process only aggregated/pseudonymized telemetry and that no identifiers or message content will be retained.

If Redwood can provide the signed addendum and DocuSign by close of business Wednesday (2026-02-18), FinCo will approve the onboarding conditioned on receipt of those documents. If not, FinCo requests that Redwood postpone onboarding for FinCo traffic and use the EU-only telemetry option (please provide pricing) until approvals are complete.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Legal – FinCo Payments
legal@finco.com
